title: Railways yet to clarify alcohol testing norms a year after Bilaspur crash
description:
The Railway Board is yet to decide whether a loco pilot is fit to operate a train if a certain amount of alcohol is detected in their blood, given the current policy requiring zero alcohol presence, a senior official has told PTI, asserting that a decision in this regard should be taken at the earliest.
The issue gained significance after a Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) investigation report noted that blood tests conducted on the running crew of two trains involved in a collision in Chhattisgarh's Bilaspur in 2025 showed alcohol concentrations ranging from 3 to 10 milligrams per 100 mL (mg/dL) of blood.
On November 4, 2025, the Gevra-Bilaspur MEMU passenger train rammed into the rear of a stationary goods train near Bilaspur, killing 12 people including the loco pilot of the passenger train and injuring around 20.
